name: Thirst stack gain energizes Rage (#5434)
contract: Thirst (706613) description: 'Generates $/10;681202s1 Rage and then increases the health costs of your spells...'. All three of 706613's own effects are aura 108 SPELL_AURA_ADD_PCT_MODIFIER (cost/crit/damage); none energizes Rage and EffectTriggerSpell is 0 on every effect, so 681202 Thirst SLS2 (SPELL_EFFECT_ENERGIZE, EffectBasePoints 49 + DieSides 1 = 50, MiscValue 1 = POWER_RAGE) was never cast when a stack was granted. Rage is stored at 10x displayed value, so 50 internal per new stack is the tooltip's 5 displayed Rage. The fix (aura_ascension_bloodmage_thirst_rage) hooks 706613's own AfterEffectApply (AURA_EFFECT_HANDLE_REAL_OR_REAPPLY_MASK), which SetStackAmount also triggers, so driving stacks directly with set_aura exercises the same Apply() path a live health-cost-cast proc would, without the confound of casting an actual health-cost spell: Bloodmoon Blast's own EffectTriggerSpell[1] (804092, SPELL_EFFECT_ENERGIZE, EffectBasePoints 39 + DieSides 61 -> a random 40-100 internal Rage) energizes Rage on every cast regardless of Thirst, which would make a cast-based Rage-delta assertion non-deterministic and unable to reliably discriminate a working fix from a missing one. Rage must rise by exactly 50 per new stack and not on any later refresh at the same stack count.

steps.label: Let spawn AI and level scaling settle
DISCRIMINATING: the first stack pays exactly 50 internal Rage (5 displayed)
DISCRIMINATING: two stacks pay exactly 100 internal Rage total
Refresh at the same stack count
A refresh at an unchanged stack count does not pay Rage again
